newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Northeast '96 net sinks on weak market.
newsitem.headline: Northeast '96 net sinks on weak market.

text.p: Northeast Electrical Transmission & Transformation Machinery Manufacturing Co Ltd said on Friday the 49 percent drop in its 1996 net profits resulted from weak demand and lower sale prices.

The company, China's largest high-voltage transmission equipment and transformer maker, on Friday posted net profits of 83.77 million yuan for 1996 against 163.45 million yuan for 1995 based on international accounting standards.

"Domestic demand for electrical transmission and transformation equipment slumped as the state slowed the pace of power plants construction," the company's 1996 annual report in the Shenzhen-based Securities Times said.
"Because of relatively weak demand, the firm trimmed sale prices of some products such as transformers to maintain competitiveness," the report said.
Turnover was 1.35 billion yuan, down 6.74 percent from 1.45 billion yuan in 1995. Earnings per share sagged to 0.096 yuan from 0.19 yuan in the previous year under international standards.
"We expect earnings to pick up in line with a market warm-up in 1997," a company official told the Hong Kong-based newsletter China Securities Bulletin.
"The value of buying orders received so far this year has topped our 1997 sales target," the official said, but declined to give any figure.
The annual report said the company planned to use 100 million yuan to upgrade technology as part of preparation for China's multi-billion-yuan Three Gorges hydropower project.
The hydropower and water conservancy project, which will dam the Yangtze River, is expected to be completed in 2009, state media have said.
